newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICANS TO GET ASIAN TIGER-STYLE EDUCATION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICANS TO GET ASIAN TIGER-STYLE EDUCATION.

text.p: South Africa is to introduce a new school system aimed at producing the kind of citizens that created the Asian Tiger economies, education officials said on Thursday.
Ihron Rensburg, acting director-general of education, told a news conference the new curriculum would be phased in from 1998 and would sweep away the current emphasis on rote learning.

"It's a clearly established international trend, particularly in the most dynamic of the East Asian Tigers, that the focus is much less on narrow skills than on a broader set of competencies that lay the platform for life-long learning," he said.
Rensburg said the aim of the new system would be to prepare people for adjustments they might have to make during their working lives as the economy restructured.
"Part of the reason for our current unemployment scenario is precisely because of narrow skilling," he said, describing the phenomenon as a threat to the stability of an industrialising society.
Education Minister Sibusisu Bengu said 52.2 percent of candidates had passed last year's high-school graduation (matriculation) examinations, compared with 43 percent the previous year.

"They have been the first matriculation examinations written on a non-racial basis. The class of 1996 must be proud to have emerged from an examination which had no racial tag attached to it," Bengu said.

But he added there was a very low pass rate in mathematics and science. "This clearly indicates there is still a lot of work to be done to improve the quality of performance in these key areas that are needed by our economy," he said.

The chairman of the parliamentary portfolio committee on education, Blade Nzimande, said the significance of the removal of the racial break-down of results of previous years was that South Africa for the first time had a clear idea of the standard of education.
"That 52.2 percent is telling us where South Africa is, and it means our country is at that level and we have to take it to higher than that, and that is the challenge," he said.
